statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-116312 (PostgreSQL MERGE can place the wrong row in a trigger transition table) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 16.16. The PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116312/, lists 16.16 as the fixed release for major version 16, the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, list this CVE, and the CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116312, lists 16 as affected before 16.16. The fix on the REL_16_STABLE branch is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/e48446c3e2c287d18722b3077e882f477d750652, which changes src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c, carries the trailer "Security: CVE-2026-116312" and is contained in the REL_16_16 tag. Alpine's postgresql16 16.16-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch upgrades to the upstream 16.16 release and lists CVE-2026-116312 under 16.16-r0 in its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. None of the Alpine patches applied in that APKBUILD change those files. The DHI postgresql16 16.16-r0 package for Alpine 3.23 is built from that APKBUILD and the upstream PostgreSQL 16.16 source tarball, and its postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 16.16 on both x86_64 and aarch64. Every earlier published build for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0) is an upstream release before 16.16, and its postgres server binary reports that older 16.x release on both architectures, so it is affected; 16.16-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-116312, inconsistent transition-capture state in MERGE on a partitioned table, which can make an AFTER trigger process the wrong new row, in 17.12. Major versions 15 to 18 are affected; 17 releases before 17.12 are affected and versions before PostgreSQL 15 are not (https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116312/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116312). The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
